subject: saving init point in samples.csv in command-line

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: saving init point in samples.csv in command-line
parts:
Marcus only fixed the optimizers.

I ran 2.0 command-line and saw the init value being
saved. But maybe I got a false positive because the first
sample was rejected.

Could you (Michael) check that it's being saved and if not,
open an issue to include the init point.

Nobody has any objections to saving the init point in the
output, do they?

It may cause an off-by-1 numbering depending on how it
gets numbered. That is, if we count it as an iteration,
we get one less iteration than we did before. If we
don't count it, then we get one too many lines in the CSV
file.

- Bob


On 10/2/13 4:00 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> If you've specified save_warmup and then I can't remember if Marcus's fix was just for the optimizers or also included samplers.

I'll look into it, but it may take a few days (lots of papers to write and I'm chugging up to Warwick twice a week to take a class on infinities or some other nonsense ;-) ).
I think the best option would be to an init block before the adaptation parameters get printed, but after the header. That'll mean changing the CSV reader (and the million or so dependent tests) but the easiest for the user.
